To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) for small datasets, using all features is the best strategy; 2) using all features is also the best strategy when the goal is to minimize the computation time and space; and 3) for large datasets, using a feature selection technique based on expected Mutual Information (eMI) is a good choice.

(a) the best feature definition strategy is to use a combination of unigrams, bigrams and trigrams with binary weighting, (b) the best feature selection strategy is to combine frequency based vocabulary trimming, expected mutual information, and part of speech tagging, and (c) the best lexicon selection strategy is to use an opinionated lexicon.

(1) for small datasets, the most useful features are negation enriched, unstemmed, binary weighted, and n-grams, and (2) for large datasets, the most important features are negation-enrichment, unstemming, n-grams, expected MI and part-of-speech.
